subject.title: Feature: force media delivery as document attachment (e.g. #doc)

question: Should OpenClaw add force-document behavior beyond the current per-call `forceDocument`/`asDocument` knobs, and if so should the public contract be `MEDIA:#doc`, a default-off channel setting, or no broader contract for now?
rationale: Current main and `v2026.6.11` already solve explicit per-call sends, while the remaining request creates either new model-facing media syntax or new channel config/default behavior that repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Keep Per-Call Canonical
options.body: Keep `--force-document` and `asDocument` as the supported contract for now and require a sponsored narrower proposal before adding syntax or config defaults.

options.title: Add `MEDIA:#doc` Syntax
options.body: Define fragment parsing and media-kind semantics in the shared media pipeline, then thread it through affected channel delivery paths with tests and live proof.

options.title: Add Channel Default
options.body: Design a default-off per-channel setting with explicit per-call override semantics, upgrade docs, and proof that existing default behavior remains intact.

recommendation.title: Keep Per-Call Canonical
recommendation.body: Keep `--force-document` and `asDocument` as the supported contract for now and require a sponsored narrower proposal before adding syntax or config defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current per-call force-document contract that the product decision would extend or intentionally keep canonical.
